solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Charge round Cornish town with a boy for days over Christmas

indicators.note: round says the charge wraps around the town's name

parts.note: a charge is a fee
St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall, written STIVES
a boy is a son

explanation.surface: A fee levied around a Cornish resort, plus a lad, over the Christmas holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' signals the container; St Ives is a seaside resort in Cornwall, England's south-western county.
explanation.definitionFit: The festive season is the holiday period spanning the days around Christmas.

clue.text: Gave Len unusually good news for Christians!

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the two words are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Len was unusually generous, which Christians greet as glad tidings.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangel is an old word for the gospel, the Christian message of good news.

clue.text: Such a fuss getting to function

parts.note: taken as written
a function is a party or social event, a do

explanation.surface: Someone makes a great fuss about going to a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a commotion or fuss, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Type of wine from Spain, under very popular label

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means Spain's letter goes below the rest

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a label is a tag
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A wine from Spain is sold under a highly popular brand label.
explanation.definitionFit: Vintage wine is from a single named year's harvest, a recognised category of wine.

clue.text: Unusual present — it's in snakeskin

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of the following word come out in a strange order

explanation.surface: An odd Christmas gift turns out to be wrapped in snakeskin.
explanation.definitionFit: A serpent is a snake, the creature whose skin is snakeskin, so it lives inside it.

clue.text: Curate's party's held up somewhere in church

indicators.note: held up says the hidden letters are read backwards
's here means has: the words before it hold the hidden answer

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The curate's festive gathering is delayed in a corner of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'held up' means read upwards: ESPA, which runs across curatE'S PArty's, turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the vaulted semicircular recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Carol's prospect for Wenceslas?

parts.note: in the carol Good King Wenceslas 'looked out' on the feast of Stephen; those words turned round make a word for a prospect

explanation.walkthrough: The Christmas carol 'Good King Wenceslas' opens with the king looking out on St Stephen's Day.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlook is a view or prospect, literally what one sees on looking out.

clue.text: Character dragged up at this time of the year?

definitions.text: Character dragged up at this time of the year?

parts.words: Character dragged up at this time of the year?
parts.note: dragged up means dressed in drag, and the comic role of a man dressed as a woman is a staple of Christmas shows

explanation.walkthrough: British Christmas pantomimes traditionally feature a man in outrageous women's clothes playing a comic older woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The dame is the cross-dressed comic lead of a seasonal British pantomime, a character played in drag.

clue.text: Heavenly sight delights shepherds

parts.note: the weather proverb says a crimson evening sky is a shepherd's delight; the surface suggests the angels at the Nativity

explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to the angels appearing to the shepherds at Bethlehem; it is the old rhyme 'red sky at night, shepherd's delight'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that a crimson sunset, a sight in the heavens, pleases shepherds by promising fine weather.

clue.text: A row about boy in pantomime role

indicators.note: about says A and the row sit around the boy

parts.note: a row is a din, a loud noise
a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: A squabble breaks out about a youngster cast in a pantomime part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; 'boy' in the surface looks like the role itself, but the answer is the whole pantomime hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The boy with the magic lamp is a favourite title role of British Christmas pantomime.

clue.text: Party wear in favour

definitions.meaning: something worn by supporters of a political party, such as a ribbon badge at an election count
a favour is a knot of ribbon worn as a badge

explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a rose-shaped ribbon badge worn by party candidates, and such a badge is also called a favour.

clue.text: Nominal attachments for the present

parts.note: nominal means bearing a name: the little labels tied to gifts saying who they are to and from

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nominal' looks like 'token' or 'trifling', but it means carrying names.
explanation.definitionFit: Gift labels naming giver and recipient are tied onto Christmas parcels.

clue.text: A bell shaped attachment to the Christmas parcel

indicators.note: shaped says the letters of these words are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A bell-shaped tag hangs from the Christmas parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaped' rearranges ABELL; the surface reads 'bell shaped' as a description.
explanation.definitionFit: A label is a tag attached to a parcel naming its addressee.

clue.text: Party drinks for children?

explanation.definitionFit: Tots means both small servings of spirits and young children.

clue.text: Christmas tree on the way, second to none

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the tree sits above the way

parts.note: a fir is the classic Christmas tree
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A Christmas tree on the road is unbeaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming first means being ahead of all others, an idiom matching second to none.

clue.text: Party-goer in right state

parts.note: to state is to aver, to assert

explanation.surface: A clubber who is in the proper condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A raver is someone who goes to raves or wild parties.

clue.text: Uneasy feeling a meal is badly cooked

indicators.note: badly cooked says these letters are mixed up like a botched dish

explanation.surface: Someone feels queasy because a meal has been badly prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaise is a general sense of unease or of being unwell.

clue.text: Want to change vital part of 8 Down

indicators.note: to change says the letters of the word before are reordered

parts.note: key means vital or crucial

explanation.surface: Someone wants to alter a vital piece of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges WANT to TWAN. Widow Twankey is the dame role in the Aladdin pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: Widow Twankey is a classic pantomime dame role, so she is one example of the 8 Down character.

clue.text: Appreciates token to have a drink

parts.note: a mark is a sign or token
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone values a voucher that entitles them to a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks up means raises in value, the sense in which assets appreciate.

clue.text: Christmas present drawer acting as a guide

definitions.text: Christmas present drawer acting as a guide

parts.words: Christmas present drawer acting as a guide
parts.note: a drawer here is one who draws or pulls, a reindeer hauling the sleigh of gifts, and one leads the team with his glowing nose

explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' suggests a chest of drawers or an artist, but it is something that pulls.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-nosed reindeer of the song guides Santa's sleigh, which carries the Christmas presents.

clue.text: Applause that's twofold back in pantomime stalls

indicators.note: in says the reversed word goes inside the theatre area

parts.note: the pit is the area of stalls on a theatre's ground floor

indicators.note: back says the word for twofold is read in reverse

parts.note: dual means twofold

explanation.surface: Ovation in the stalls at the pantomime comes twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals the reversal and 'in' the container; in a British theatre the pit is the ground-floor seating behind the orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is an expression of praise, originally a round of applause.

clue.text: Christmas gift offer

definitions.meaning: to offer is to hand over formally, to proffer

explanation.definitionFit: Present means both a gift and, as a verb, to offer or hand over.

clue.text: Dad has to get hold of a superior card — it solves all problems

indicators.note: has to get hold of says Dad wraps around what follows

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad
an is the indefinite article, a form of a
an ace is the top card in many games

explanation.surface: Father needs to grab a winning card to sort out every difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to get hold of' signals the container; 'a' stands for the longer form of the indefinite article here.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a cure-all, a remedy for every ill.

clue.text: Ten fuddled with drink weave around

indicators.note: fuddled means muddled, as if by drink, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: wine is a drink

explanation.surface: Ten people, befuddled by alcohol, stagger around.
explanation.definitionFit: To entwine is to twist or weave things around one another.

clue.text: Two parties and there's nothing left of the bird!

definitions.text: there's nothing left of the bird!

indicators.note: two says the word for a party appears twice

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: After two parties, the turkey has been entirely eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo is the extinct flightless bird, so none of its kind remains.

clue.text: A favourite place to get spirits?

definitions.meaning: ghosts frequenting a place, the question mark marking the playful sense

explanation.definitionFit: Haunt names a place frequented often, and as a verb is what ghosts do to a house.

clue.text: It may hold needles on the tree — but only as a present

definitions.text: It may hold needles on the tree — but only as a present

parts.words: It may hold needles on the tree — but only as a present
parts.note: needles suggests pine needles, but it is a small sewing case, which would only be on the tree as a hung gift

explanation.walkthrough: 'needles' suggests the Christmas tree's foliage, but these are sewing needles.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles and similar sewing items.

clue.text: They were wise, putting scholar before soldier

indicators.note: putting before says the scholar comes ahead of the soldier

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar's degree
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: The wise people put learning ahead of military service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi are the Wise Men who visited the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Plan to put money in the drinks kitty

indicators.note: put in says the money goes inside the kitty

parts.note: a pot is a shared fund, a kitty
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Someone plans to add cash to the pub kitty.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a scheme or plan, often a secret one.

clue.text: Mother left fat on duck

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: Mum has left fat on the roast duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallard is the common wild duck.

clue.text: Child so wrapped up in wintry weather like this

indicators.note: wrapped up suggests bundled about, so the letters of the phrase are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A child is bundled up warmly against the winter weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Coldish means somewhat cold, as winter weather tends to be.

clue.text: In the festive season one gets all dressed up to sit in the living room

definitions.text: In the festive season one gets all dressed up to sit in the living room

parts.words: In the festive season one gets all dressed up to sit in the living room
parts.note: dressed up suggests a party guest, but here it means decorated with baubles and lights

explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed up' and 'living room' suggest a guest, but the thing decorated is a fir standing in the lounge.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorated fir is set up in homes over the festive period, adorned with ornaments.
